draft.title: Class actions
card: A class action is one civil claim brought by one person for a whole group. Seven or more people must have claims against the same defendant, the claims must arise from related circumstances, and they must raise a common issue of law or fact.
The person who starts it is the lead plaintiff. They act for the group members, who are usually not named in the case and do not each have to appear in court.
Costs are shared across the group. A person with a small loss, who could not afford to sue alone, may be able to have their claim heard.
The court deals with the common issues once, instead of in many separate cases. This can save time and avoid different results for similar claims.
draft.remember: One lead plaintiff, one case for many people, with costs shared.

a.q: Why can a class action give access to justice to a person with a small loss?
opts: The group shares the costs of one case
The lead plaintiff pays the costs alone
Each member gets a separate hearing for free
The court lowers the loss needed to sue
a.why: The costs of one case are spread across the group, so a person with a small loss does not face the full expense alone. The lead plaintiff does not have to carry the whole cost, and members do not get separate hearings.
a.clue: Think about who pays when many people share one case.

b.q: Hundreds of customers of a Geelong energy company were each overcharged a small amount by the same billing error. Which is the best reason a class action suits them?
opts: Their similar claims can be heard together in one case
Each customer must appear and give evidence in court
Each customer will win a larger amount than alone
The company must admit it was at fault to the group
b.why: The claims arise from the same error, so the common issue can be decided once, and the costs are shared. Members do not each have to appear, and a class action does not guarantee a larger payment or an admission of fault.
b.clue: Look for what the claims have in common.

a.best: The group shares the costs of one case

b.best: Their similar claims can be heard together in one case

problems.detail: The clue 'who pays when many people share one case' echoes the word 'shares' in the right option, so a student could match the words without knowing the idea.
